newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bonds firm after German data, crown gains.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bonds firm after German data, crown gains.

text.p: 1535 GMT - Swedish debt yields fell slightly on the back of higher than expected German unemployment figures and the crown gained strength against the softer mark.
Dealers expect the crown to firm further against the mark.
* Six month T-bill rate up one basis point to 4.30 pct
* 10-year bond yield down two basis points to 6.55 pct
* Mark softens to 4.2910 against crown vs 4.2950 Tuesday
Long Swedish bond yields fell slightly on Wednesday on the back of higher than expected German unemployment figures and the crown gained strength against the softer mark.
The 10-year bond yield slid two basis points to 6.55 percent, while the six-month T-bill rate rose one basis point to 4.30 percent.
"The fall in Swedish bond yields was completely driven by foreign trends. The time was ripe for a recoil," a trader said.
The crown firmed somewhat to 4.2910 against the mark from 4.2950 late on Tuesday, helped by the dollar.
Dealers expected the crown to keep strengthening.
"The dollar should rise to 1.90 mark. That makes me beleive that the crown will at least make a test down to 4.25 to the mark," a trader said.
"Generally speaking the crown should firm, unless there are any large political changes, as Swedish fundamentals look good."
